title: Up Strums for Beginners: Thin-pick technique, muted practice, and thinnest-string focus (JustinGuitar)
summary: This JustinGuitar beginner lesson explains up strums (upstrokes) as the in-between motion to the standard down strum. The video emphasizes using an ultra-thin pick to facilitate clean upstrokes, teaching muted practice to avoid noise, and clarifying that upstrokes typically strike only the thinnest three or four strings. Through slow, counted practice (one-and-two-and-three-and-four-and) with optional foot tapping for rhythm, the instructor guides learners to coordinate rhythm with the strum direction, gradually transitioning from muting to actual strumming on the guitar. The lesson also contrasts strumming all strings versus focusing on the thinnest strings for clearer, more musical results, especially when working with common chords like D minor and A minor. A preview of upcoming strumming patterns that incorporate upstrokes signals progression beyond the basics.

sections.description: Justin introduces up strums, compares them to down strums, and stresses the benefit of using a very thin pick (0.38 mm nylon) to facilitate smooth upstrokes. He also notes a left-handed student anecdote about the pick thickness influencing difficulty.
